newsitem.title: CHINA: McDonald's shuts flagship China store.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's shuts flagship China store.

text.p: U.S. hamburger giant McDonald's shut the doors of its flagship China store on Monday after reaching an agreement to allow the outlet to be razed to make way for a huge shopping plaza, company officials said.
"We have an agreement with the government for the relocation of the store," said Tim Lai, general manager of Beijing McDonald's Food Co Ltd.
"Over the last two years we discussed with the city government...and came to an agreement about a month ago," Lai said.

McDonald's had agreed to move the restaurant, one of the largest in the world and its first to open in China, to make way for a renovation of the street to include a commercial and shopping complex to be built by Hong Kong's Cheung Kong (Holdings), Lai said.

The fast-food chain would receive compensation for the move and could possibly open a store within the new shopping centre, Lai said but declined to give further details of the compensation agreement.
